content.text:
### Source
Git history and PR #93; supplied design/revision notes treated as the implementing agent’s own decision record, not independent evidence.

### What I searched
Read baseline `8bc7855`, initial tracing `8d87a49`, correction `e4f9be4`; their error/conversion/tracing diffs; PR #93 body, comments and reviews. Ran `git log --all -G '#\[.*instrument' -- exposed/src` and `rg '#\[.*instrument' exposed/src`; neither found attribute use/history. Read design.md and revision-todo.md fully.

### Direct evidence

- [PR #93](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/93): “error conversion discards unexpected service causes.” The stated objective was retaining causes and one terminal logger. Its current body says: “One exhaustive HTTP mapping owns status and diagnostic category.”
- [design.md](/tmp/exposed-http-tracing-design/design.md:71): “Handler conversion implementations are removed in favor of typed From derivations.” Same paragraph explicitly chooses canonical domain wrappers and a private response extension to retain diagnostics. This is the agent’s stated rationale for the revision, not proof that wrapping was required.
- [design.md](/tmp/exposed-http-tracing-design/design.md:111): “No anyhow payload, generic source escape hatch, or HTTP error downcast remains.” This documents what the correction optimized for.
- [revision-todo.md](/tmp/exposed-http-tracing-design/revision-todo.md:14): “The implementation added a blanket error/warn macro ban to enforce ownership, then used event! to bypass its own restriction.” This addresses **event macros only**, not `#[instrument]`.
- [design.md](/tmp/exposed-http-tracing-design/design.md:114): “Standard tracing error!, warn!, info!, debug! macros are selected by outcome and share one field list.” Again, the documented correction interpreted “macros” as event emission macros.

### Mechanical history, not motivation

- [Baseline error.rs](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/8bc78555f9a68b7148846fc207465fae319bc202/exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/error.rs#L9) already modeled HTTP outcomes: `InternalServerError`, `NotFound`, `UnprocessibleEntity(String)`.
- Baseline mappings lived in [handlers.rs](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/8bc78555f9a68b7148846fc207465fae319bc202/exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/handlers.rs#L80) and [entity_details.rs](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/8bc78555f9a68b7148846fc207465fae319bc202/exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/handlers/entity_details.rs#L27). They exhaustively converted domain variants into HTTP outcomes, but discarded unexpected causes.
- [Initial commit](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/commit/8d87a49de4c7e4784e1f238b6805b9450643b1db) retained HTTP variants, added `anyhow::Error` to the internal variant, and downcast causes to select diagnostic categories.
- [Correction](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/commit/e4f9be4078fc291391d259ac9bbee657d12a7f44) replaced HTTP outcome variants with `Search(EntitySearchError)` / `Details(EntityDetailsError)`, deleted the explicit conversions, and moved exhaustive mapping into `classification()`. Therefore the current shape was introduced by the typed-error correction; it was not an existing application convention inherited from baseline.
- Current [tracing.rs:37–64](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-http-tracing/exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/tracing.rs:37) manually creates the request span and attaches it with `.instrument(span)`. It dynamically selects DEBUG for health, INFO otherwise. This is an implementation fact; no retrieved author statement says those needs ruled out `#[instrument]`.

### Gaps and contradictions
PR #93 has no comments or reviews. No searched commit, PR text, or supplied rationale compares manual instrumentation with `#[instrument]`, or records rejecting the attribute. The evidence supports “the revision addressed event macros” and **does not support** “we evaluated the attribute and chose against it.”

The design record claims the user “approved” and “corrected” choices, but these are the agent’s summaries. They cannot establish the exact scope of the user’s original words.
